subject: English
title: Year 7 English: Half-term 1 (Reading fiction: inference and atmosphere)

questions.question:
Read the passage.

"The attic had not been opened for years. When Leo finally forced the door, a breath of cold, dusty air rolled out to meet him. Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals. In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

What atmosphere does the writer create?
questions.explanation: Dust, cold air, crouching shapes and a mysterious ticking build tension.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

"The attic had not been opened for years. When Leo finally forced the door, a breath of cold, dusty air rolled out to meet him. Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals. In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

"Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals" is an example of a ...
questions.explanation: It compares the shapes to animals using 'like', so it is a simile.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

"The attic had not been opened for years. When Leo finally forced the door, a breath of cold, dusty air rolled out to meet him. Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals. In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

Why might the writer use the verb "crouched"?
options: To show the shapes are comfortable
To show the attic is tidy
To suggest the shapes might be ready to spring
questions.answer: To suggest the shapes might be ready to spring
questions.explanation: Crouching is what an animal does before it pounces, which adds threat.

questions.question:

"The attic had not been opened for years. When Leo finally forced the door, a breath of cold, dusty air rolled out to meet him. Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals. In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

"He did not believe himself." What does this suggest about Leo?
options: He is sure it is a clock
He is lying to someone else
questions.explanation: He tries to calm himself but doubts it, showing fear.

In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

Why does the writer end with a very short sentence?
options: Because the writer ran out of ideas
To create a sudden, uneasy ending
questions.answer: To create a sudden, uneasy ending
questions.explanation: A short final sentence has impact and leaves the reader uneasy.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

"The attic had not been opened for years. When Leo finally forced the door, a breath of cold, dusty air rolled out to meet him. Shapes crouched under white sheets like sleeping animals. In the far corner, something ticked: slow, patient, waiting. Leo told himself it was only a clock. He did not believe himself."

In "slow, patient, waiting", the clock is described as if it were alive. This is ...
questions.explanation: Being patient and waiting are human qualities, so this is personification.

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to "ominous"?
questions.explanation: Ominous means suggesting something bad is about to happen.

questions.question: "I crept down the stairs, my heart pounding." What narrative perspective is this?
questions.explanation: 'I' shows a first-person narrator telling their own story.

questions.question: What is a third-person narrator?
questions.explanation: Third person describes characters from outside, using he/she/they.

questions.question: A writer says a character 'slammed the door and stomped upstairs'. What does this SHOW rather than tell?
questions.explanation: The actions reveal anger without the writer stating it.

questions.question: Choose the best word to replace "walked" to show someone is nervous.
Why do writers often describe the weather at the start of a story?
options: To set the mood and atmosphere
questions.answer: To set the mood and atmosphere
questions.explanation: Weather is a quick way to create mood, e.g. a storm for tension.
